US$2006: Table 1 ('Performance & Costs (US$ 2006)', 'mln $2006') and Table 2 ('Costs (US$ 2006)'); p.1 '(US$ 2006)'. The Table 2 projections state no year (US$2006 assumed). The coal price ($37/ton) has no year stated.

Main file: three examples. (1) Table 1, the NETL commercial-scale FT plant on Illinois No. 6 coal (gasifier_coal_fischer-tropsch, serving gasifier_coal-to-liquids): capacity 50,000 bbl/d, availability, overnight capex per bbl/d. (2) Table 2 CTL and (3) Table 2 GTL (reactor_natural-gas_fischer-tropsch, serving reactor_gas-to-liquids): each ONE example with three size cases (800, 2400, 4800 MWth; 10,000-60,000 bbl/d) named in square brackets at the start of each row note; capacity (syncrude GJ/h), DERIVED liquid-product efficiency (syncrude/energy input), capex, fixed O&M DERIVED from '4%/yr of capital cost', variable O&M, CO2 and CH4 emissions per PJ output, plus merged construction time, lifetime and load factor. Sidecars (not loaded): _netl-plant (Table 1 mass/energy and capex components - daily rates with no per-unit basis in GJ or t, so no flows file), _sizes-and-inputs (MWth ratings, energy input, bbl/d, power-system MWel, land use), _projections, _ccs-cost-adders, _economics-and-market (feed prices, ROI, DCL yields, market figures, reactor temperatures). Direct coal liquefaction has no archetype and only yields: sidecar. Utility power is not covered by the brief.

(1) Table 1 prints '81.400' ($/bbl/d) with a thousands DOT while the same table uses thousands commas ('4,070', '24,533'); it is 81,400. (2) Table 2 'Capacity, output MWth' (800/2400/4800) does not equal the syncrude output (2400 GJ/h = 667 MW, etc.), even with the power-generation system added. (3) The same nominal output (10,000 bbl/d) is 2,400 GJ/h for CTL but 2,750 GJ/h for GTL. (4) Table 2 capex ($/GJ output) does not reconcile with Table 1: NETL's $81,400/(bbl/d) is about $39 per GJ/yr on Table 2's energy content, against 10.5-22.7 for CTL; the basis cannot be verified. (5) Text says a GTL plant costs 'approximately half' a CTL plant; Table 2 puts GTL capex at about one third. (6) The NETL plant captures 32,481 t/d CO2 while Table 2's emissions are without CCS. (7) The references cite 'ETSAP Technology Brief S01 Production of Syngas from Coal'; that brief is P05. (8) Merged cells across the three size columns: construction time, lifetime, load factor, fixed O&M, land use, CCS reduction. (9) The projection capex ranges (2020/2030/2050) are each 0.88-0.97 x the current range of the 800/2400/4800 MWth size column in the same position, so the time trend may be the size effect copied across; '15 -22' and '3.5 -4.5' are printed with a detached minus. (10) Text mixes number formats: '160.000 t/y', '0,22 GWth'. (11) Plant output 50,000 bbl/d vs naphtha + diesel 49,992.
